messages.subject: Aggregated site visits/occasions
parts:
Hi, 

I have almost a decade of citizen science bird survey count data at some 20+ sites. I was hoping to use AH models to analyse abundance and occupancy over the years. However, I have one significant issue that I hope can be overcome in some way. I.e. during each site visit multiple observers sampled a site, which i believe could be construed as separate sampling occasion. The problem is that each observers species counts have been aggregated into one list for each site per year. As this violates the modeling requirements of at least 2 sampling occasions per site per season I am wondering if someone can suggest a solution to this issue? As I understand, this will implications of the calculation of detection probability? Is this a deal breaker? Or is it a case of using a different statistical approach? 

Many thanks 

Alex

messages.author: 02d195331194f5bd
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Aggregated site visits/occasions
parts:
A few thoughts: 
  • Option 1: use open-population models (see here and here). These are implemented in unmarked via the pcountOpen function. 
  • Option 2: use models that do not require replicate sampling (see here). You can fit these models in the 'detect' R package using the svabu and svocc functions 
    • Note that these models can be very sensitive to model assumptions and so might give very biased estimates (see here and here). 
  • Option 3: use Poisson regression models that do not explicitly estimate absolute abundance (see here). You could still model variation in detectability and abundance through space or time, you just won't get estimates of absolute abundance. 
  • Option 4: use all 3 of the above methods and see if they give similar results. If they do, great! If they don't, you'll need to think more about why some of the models are biased/inaccurate.
Philip Shirk
